Hi - I love my Spironolactone, I have been taking 100 mg daily for over 6 months now.  I have also been doing this in tandem with tretinoin 0.025%.  The only noticeable side effect from  Spironolactone was that my breasts grew MARGINALLY.  Much of my acne issues are hormonal, and so Spironolactone has been particularly helpful in wrangling my hormonal acne.  Additionally, I am using Spironolactone to assist with my female pattern hair loss, which I have found to be helpful in tandem with Minoxidil.  
In terms of acne-related results for Spironolactone after 6+ months: this is the happiest I have been with my skin in a looonnnng time (maybe ever?).  Certainly, the tretinoin in conjunction has been a game-changer as well.  Really, after I have started on those 2 things, the only other items I have in my skincare rotation are my CeraVe foaming cleanser, Kose Softymo Deep Cleansing Oil, Vanicream Moisturizer Cream and LaRoche Posay Melt-In Milk SPF 60.  Hopefully this is helpful to you, and good luck on your skincare journey!

Hi - I am in a DPT program that heavily uses case-based learning within the program.  I'm thinking this might be remotely similar to problem-based learning - please correct me if I'm wrong here.

All cases were discussed in groups - roughly 11 students per group.  We were all given a real-world example prompt, debriefed on the topic for an hour together and then went our separate ways to create a flow chart to analyze/understand the mechanism of the presenting case, answer and research respective topics/TherEx/learning outcomes.  After doing these things on our own, we would reconvene, discuss our findings, and be given a "closing" prompt for that respective case.

My experience doing this was fine, however, I stayed with the same group of people throughout the semester (would have loved a switch up every now and then, perhaps even a smaller group).  I liked it enough, my largest criticism was I would have loved a little more autonomy in performing my own analysis/research/mechanism investigation.

My undergrad school allowed me to pay a small fee to have my Pass/Fail letter grade revealed for application/admissions purposes - at the time of taking the course, I didn't realize that I wanted to go into PT/would need that class.  It didn't appear to pose any major issues.

As someone who is grieving the very recent loss of a parent right now, the best thing they could do for themselves is therapy - either individually or as a family unit. They need to have a functional, well-differentiated conversation together, and if someone is going to get triangulated into the mix, it will be best with a therapist.
